Seminar Title:

Finite-sample inference for comparing quantiles across several normal populations: A Simulation Study

Seminar Type:

Abstract:

We investigate the problem of testing the equality of a specified quantile across several normal populations and compare seven competing procedures: approximate test (AT), generalized variable test (GVT), asymptotic likelihood ratio test (ALRT), standardized likelihood ratio test (SLRT), parametric bootstrap likelihood ratio test (PBLRT), and two computational approach tests (CAT1 and CAT2). Their finite-sample performance is evaluated through extensive Monte Carlo simulations in terms of empirical type I error and statistical power across a range of sample-size configurations, parameter settings, and quantile levels. The results reveal distinct finite-sample performance patterns across the competing procedures, with size and power varying with the quantile level and underlying parameter configuration. Three real-data applications further demonstrate the practical utility of the considered methods. Overall, the study provides a comprehensive finite-sample assessment of quantile equality tests and offers practical guidance for reliable inference across several normal populations
